title: Unraveling Nanodiffraction Patterns of Metal Halide Perovskite Nanowires Inside Carbon Nanotubes
content: Possessing ideal properties for use in solar cells, CO2 reduction, and hydrogen production, metal halide perovskites (MHPs) are heavily researched materials [1]. However, at room temperature many MHPs undergo crystallographic phase transitions triggered by light or moisture, to crystal phases with less ideal band gaps or structural degradation [2][3]. Probing and identifying the crystal phase of MHPs under different conditions is critical to the research and development of halide perovskites which are stable at room temperature. While many methods of characterization exist, nanoscale MHPs, especially those under 5nm, are weakly scattering and sensitive to x-ray and electron probes and are hard to characterize using conventional methods [4].
